the short version of the story is that a group of hackers working under the label "anonymous" acquired internal emails from a company called HBGary Federal that revealed to the public that they basically create and manage sockpuppet accounts and solutions for governments and companies that want to control public opinion through black propaganda online, and that they had engaged in business agreements with the US federal government relating to this solution. This event is when "astroturf" became a sort of household term. Previously accounts like this were just called propagandists or shills most of the time.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astroturfing

edit: to put it simply, HB Gary was one company that basically did vote brigades and comments online in a way that made it look like a LOT of people felt a particular way about this or that issue or policy or content when they really didn't. The leak verified that it was a real thing and that the federal government was using it. It proves that its not just a nutcase "conspiracy theory", and that social media sites that want everyone to be on a level playing field MUST try to combat it.
